name: adv_sac_bad
title: Soft Actor-Critic: twin critics, a Polyak target and a tuned temperature - ten planted defects
origin: the defective twin of adv_sac_clean, hardening round 2, 2026-09-14
note: The off-policy actor-critic shape round 1 did not reach: three optimizers stepping in one function body, a target network, and a replay buffer. `unsupported` rows are planted defects no rule's documented detection covers today; they are recorded so they can be promoted the day a rule sees them. Two of them are the round-2 findings DGRG-14 (MLV203 does not follow the one module-local call hop MLV201/MLV202 follow, so a step-before-backward inside `update()` is invisible and undeclared) and DGRG-16 (`env.reset(seed=...)` silences MLV601 workspace-wide).

expected.defect: the two Q networks live in a plain Python list comprehension
expected.why: neither critic is registered on TwinCritic, so critic.parameters() is empty and torch.optim.Adam(critic.parameters()) optimises nothing at all
the actor trunk carries nn.Dropout(0.1), so every deterministic evaluation episode is scored with 10% of the trunk dropped

expected.defect: the evaluation episodes are not wrapped in torch.no_grad()
expected.why: a full autograd graph is built for every step of every evaluation episode and thrown away

expected.defect: the device is hard-coded to cuda with no torch.cuda.is_available() check
expected.why: the script cannot start at all on a CPU-only machine, which is where most of this corpus is read

expected.defect: the whole actor module is pickled instead of its state_dict
expected.why: the checkpoint carries the class path, so it stops loading as soon as the file moves

expected.defect: nothing seeds torch, numpy or random; the only seed in the file is env.reset(seed=...), which seeds the gymnasium environment and nothing else
expected.why: the network initialisation, the reparameterised action sampling and the replay index draw all move between runs, so the learning curve is not reproducible. MLView is silent here: finding DGRG-16

forbidden.why: every backward() in update() (lines 133, 140, 149) is outside a no_grad block; the only no_grad here is the action selection at line 215
no softmax is applied anywhere and there is no cross-entropy of any kind; the losses are F.mse_loss and two means
there is no binary cross-entropy in this project
every tensor is created with device=DEVICE and the replay buffer allocates on the same device; there is no DataLoader to move a batch from
there is no train/test split call in this project at all
SquashedGaussianActor.__init__ and TwinCritic.__init__ both call super().__init__() on their first line (lines 37 and 66)
there is no DataLoader in this project; the replay buffer is indexed with torch.randint
there is no DataLoader in this project

unsupported.defect: critic_opt.step() at line 132 runs before critic_loss.backward() at line 133, in the same block
unsupported.why: MLV203 iterates `ctx.loops("batch")` and reads only calls lexically inside that loop, so a training step factored into `def update(...)` is never judged - and no coverage diagnostic is emitted either, because `note_untagged_loop` requires the calls to sit in some loop. See finding DGRG-14.

unsupported.defect: the actor update never calls actor_opt.zero_grad(), so every actor step applies the sum of every actor gradient computed since the run started
unsupported.why: MLV201 anchors on the innermost for over a LOADER-tagged value; an off-policy RL script has no DataLoader by construction.

unsupported.defect: running_critic is created at line 202, outside both loops, and accumulates the live critic loss that update() returns
unsupported.why: MLV205's `_loss_operand` looks for a LOSS-tagged NAME in the accumulation expression; the right-hand side here is a call to a workspace function, and the rule does not follow the callee's return the way `ir/returns.py` does for backward().

unsupported.defect: soft_update() is defined, documented and never called, so the target critic stays at its initialisation for the whole run and the bootstrap target never improves
unsupported.why: no rule models `a target network that is never synchronised`; it is the single most common SAC/DQN implementation bug.

unsupported.defect: the bootstrap target is computed with gradients on and never detached, so the critic is trained through its own target
unsupported.why: no rule models `a target tensor reaching a loss without .detach()`.

unsupported.defect: the transitions produced by the evaluation episodes are pushed into the training replay buffer, so the agent trains on its own evaluation rollouts
unsupported.why: MLV101/MLV102 model an sklearn transformer fitted on the wrong rows; an RL replay buffer filled from the evaluation environment is the same defect in a shape no rule reads.

unsupported.defect: log_alpha is detached inside its own loss, so alpha_loss has no gradient path to the only parameter alpha_opt owns and the entropy temperature never moves
unsupported.why: no rule models `an optimizer whose parameters are unreachable from the loss it steps on`.
